q1.explanationZh: 男孩说板球不能选，他还是打网球，并邀请女孩一起（Why don’t you join me at tennis?），女孩同意了（OK, why not?）。B 板球不是可选的运动；C 女孩本来想打排球，最后决定放学后在公园里玩排球。

q2.explanationZh: 男孩说他喜欢交通展区那辆车轮很特别的老式自行车（that old-fashioned bike with unusual wheels）。A 带狮子的旧壶他觉得很奇怪；B 喜欢那把大椅子的是女孩。

q3.explanationZh: 男孩说如果非得这样，不带笔记本电脑也行（I can manage without my laptop），因为平板电脑更省地方。A 相机可以挂在脖子上带走；C 平板电脑占地方小，他要带上。

q4.explanationZh: 小长颈鹿已经不喝奶、开始吃树叶，但还够不着，所以长颈鹿妈妈要把树叶从树上拽下来喂它（the mother has to pull them off the tree to feed her baby）。B 喂它的是妈妈，不是人；C 小长颈鹿还够不着树叶，不能自己吃。

q5.explanationZh: 老师建议把牛奶、草莓和冰块混在一起做奶昔，男孩说“我就做这个！”（I’ll do that!）。A 胡萝卜蛋糕是他妈妈以前做的；B 豆子汉堡是他以前帮朋友做的。

q6.explanationZh: 女孩说她们只走了照片上的那一段路，提到湖边的风特别大（how strong the wind was by the lake）。B 西海岸那座高楼林立的城市太远，她们没去；A 那片有巨石的大沙漠是她希望以后能去看的。

q7.explanationZh: 他们平时坐火车，但火车司机罢工了；家里的车上周坏了，爸爸想过租车，最后决定坐长途大巴（we decided to go by coach）。A 车坏了，没开车；C 火车司机在罢工。

q8.explanationZh: 演出取消是因为领舞身体不舒服回家了（the lead dancer’s had to go home），而且没人练过她的部分。A 他们已经把舞台上方的灯修好了；B 乐队成员下周有体育比赛，影响的是下周，不是今晚。

q9.explanationZh: 女孩说能理解数学作业多，但她认为老师不应该每一科都布置作业（I don’t think teachers ought to give it for every subject），也就是只有某些科目该有作业。A 她没说低年级学生不该有作业；C 她觉得数学作业多是可以理解的。

q10.explanationZh: 男孩花了整个周末想通关，几个小时都过不了第一个怪物（I was really stuck!），还说不喜欢太简单的游戏，说明这个游戏玩起来有挑战性。A 他一开始看不懂玩法说明；C 他只是说花很多钱买游戏又很快玩完很烦人，没说这个游戏不贵。

q11.explanationZh: 女孩说羽毛球很好玩，男孩一定会喜欢，提议一起打（We should play.），是在建议一项活动。B 这里的 sorry 是遗憾男孩没能来，不是道歉；C 周一放学后一起去是新的约定，不是提醒原来的安排。

q12.explanationZh: 男孩提议挂气球和彩灯，女孩想先问问父母，怕弄坏东西，男孩同意“最好问一下”（Probably best to ask），所以他们需要就布置房间征求意见。B 哥哥只是教他怎么连接音箱，不是帮他们选音乐；C 大家各带一道菜，食物不需要建议。

q13.explanationZh: 女孩说教练知道她快康复了，很快就能回到球队比赛（it won’t be long before I’m back playing with the team again），她对此很有信心。B 她知道自己不能上场是因为腿受了伤；C 她要去给队友加油，并不嫉妒。

q14.explanationZh: Mona 说有些记者在大学学新闻学，或政治、经济等，而她学的是历史（I did history）。journalism、politics、economics 都是别的记者学的。

q15.explanationZh: 她的第一篇文章上了头版，但只是关于一条新路（it was only about a new road）。银行抢劫和名人婚礼是她说当时没有机会写的事。

q16.explanationZh: 大多数记者离不开笔记本电脑，但她走到哪儿都带着一支笔（I take a pen wherever I go）。手机她丢过很多次，纸她总能找到东西代替。

q17.explanationZh: 下次采访的人来自一家大型运输公司，不是老板也不是经理，而是一位卡车司机（it’s with a lorry driver）。politician 是她上一次采访的人。

q18.explanationZh: 有人认为声音洪亮或外表整洁重要，但她认为真正有帮助的是记忆力（it’s my memory that really helps）。

q19.explanationZh: 她要写的书探讨如何利用太阳产生我们需要的能源（how we can use the sun to produce it）。石油、风和海只是她顺便提到的。

q20.explanationZh: 是学校的一位老师给他看了救助中心的广告（It was one of my school teachers who’d shown me the advert for it）。B 妈妈对他出远门很担心；A 好朋友只是支持他，帮他说服妈妈。

q21.explanationZh: 镇上新开了一家冲浪板店，他在那里找到了工作（I got a job there），攒够了钱。A 叔叔愿意借钱给他，但他想自己付；C 他想过在网上卖东西，但最后没有必要这样做。

q22.explanationZh: 他说工作人员和其他志愿者的欢迎非常热情，让他永远难忘（The welcome I got from the staff and the other volunteers was brilliant）。C 他到的时候大象都睡了，第二天才知道有二十多头；A 天太黑，他没能看花园。

q23.explanationZh: 他的第一份工作是把大象要吃的东西放进桶里（put all the stuff that the elephants were going to eat in buckets）。C 给大象洗澡他只能在旁边看；B 和兽医一起工作需要专业资格。

q24.explanationZh: 他认识了很多人，但很难听懂他们说的话（it wasn’t easy to understand what they were saying）。B 他以为炎热会很难受，结果还好；A 日出时起床开工很凉快，他没说早起难。

q25.explanationZh: 他早就读到过大象聪明、记性好，但直到和它们相处后才发现每头大象都不一样（no two elephants are the same），有的勇敢，有的害羞。C 记性好是他之前就知道的；A 他没说大象彼此很友善。

content.v: Test Two. There are four parts to the test. You will hear each part twice. We will now stop for a moment. Please ask any questions now because you must not speak during the test.
Now look at the instructions for Part One.
For each question, choose the correct answer. Look at question one.
One. Which sport will the girl do next term?
Have you decided which sport to do next term? We have to tell the teacher.
I love watching cricket – I’d really like to try that.
Is cricket an option? That’d be fun.
Afraid not. I suppose I’ll do tennis again.
You’re good at that, aren’t you? I was thinking of volleyball.
Lots of people do that – it’s very difficult to get into the school team. Why don’t you join me at tennis?
I’ve never tried it – but OK, why not? We can always play volleyball in the park after school.
Two. Which object in the museum did the boy like?
I didn’t think I’d enjoy that museum – but it was great.
I didn’t like much of the stuff actually… apart from something I saw in the transport section.
You mean the old train?
I was thinking of that old-fashioned bike with unusual wheels.
Oh, right. Did you see that big old pot with the lion on? It’s really valuable.
I thought it looked pretty strange. And I didn’t think much of the furniture, either.
Oh, but I loved the enormous chair.
I read it was designed for kings to sit on.
Three. What does the boy decide to leave behind?
I can’t fit everything in my suitcase, Mum.
I’m not surprised, you don’t need to take a tablet and your laptop!
But I like reading on one and watching films on the other. I’ve got my camera in there, too.
But it’s quite big. Can’t you hang it round your neck?
That’ll help, I guess. I can manage without my laptop if I’ve got to. The tablet takes up less room. But I’m going to have to pack my case again, I think.
Don’t worry. I’ll give you a hand.
Four. What is the baby giraffe doing?

Here we have our newest giraffe in the wildlife park! The staff are very happy with her progress. Giraffes are pretty big, so they need lots of food! Babies start drinking milk within the first hour of their lives. They feed on this for the next few months – this little giraffe’s just finished that part of her life. Later, the baby giraffe begins eating leaves. As you can see, the mother has to pull them off the tree to feed her baby as very young giraffes can’t reach them yet!
Five. What does the boy decide to make in the cookery lesson?
You can choose what to make using fruit and vegetables in tomorrow’s cookery lesson. Any questions?
But I don’t like the taste of them …
You can make them delicious, like those milk drinks in fast food places! Just mix milk, strawberries and ice.
I’ll do that! My mum once made a cake with carrots and I liked that.
Making cakes with vegetables is a great way to get them into your diet…
Yeah! I helped my friend make some burgers from beans once! They were good!
See? It’s easy!
Six. Where did the girl go on holiday?
How was your holiday?

Cool! We did a road trip in the USA. Well, actually we only did the part of it you can see in this photo. You wouldn’t believe how strong the wind was by the lake, which was huge. The road went all the way off to the city on the west coast. It’s famous for its skyscrapers. That was too far for us to go, though. The road also passes through a big desert where there are enormous rocks – I’d love to see that one day.
Seven. How did the boy travel to his aunt’s house?
What did you do at the weekend?
My dad and I went to visit my aunt.
Is her house near here?
Not really. She lives quite a long way away, by the sea. We usually go by train, but the train drivers were on strike.
So did your dad drive?
Well, our car broke down last week and Dad thought about hiring another one, but in the end, we decided to go by coach. It was nearly as fast as going by car. Anyway, I slept most of the journey.
That is the end of Part One.
Now look at Part Two. For each question, choose the correct answer.
Eight. You will hear a boy telling his friend about a school show.
Have you heard? They’ve cancelled tonight’s school show.
Oh, no! Was there a problem with the sound system for the music again?
Actually, the lead dancer’s had to go home because she wasn’t feeling well. Nobody else has practised her part and she’s on stage in almost every scene.
What a shame!
I know! And we worked so hard to get those lights above the stage working properly.
I hope it’ll go ahead soon. But it can’t be next week – quite a few members of the orchestra have got a sports competition then, so they’ll be busy with that.
Oh, right.
Nine. You will hear two friends talking about homework.
I’ve got so much homework. It gets more and more as I get older. This week I’ve got so much for geography, IT and maths.
Well, we have to study more subjects than younger students, I suppose.

True, but at our age, we have loads of other things to do too, like helping out at home. I never had to do that when I was eight. I can see why we get so much homework for a subject like maths, but I don’t think teachers ought to give it for every subject we do.
No, I agree.
Ten. You will hear two friends talking about a computer game.
Have you played that game Monsterfun yet?
I spent all weekend trying to complete it! I couldn’t understand the information about how to play at first.
Nor me, but I’m nearly at the last level!
Really? I’ve spent hours trying to get past the first monster!
Oh – you go through a cave behind some rocks.
That makes sense. I was really stuck! Anyway, I don’t like games that are too simple.
I know. Some are so easy you’ve finished in a couple of hours!
Yes. It’s annoying to pay a lot for a game, and then finish it quickly.
True!
Eleven. You will hear a girl and a boy talking about a sports centre.
Hi, how was the sports centre?
Good, thanks. I’m sorry you couldn’t come.
What did you do there?
Badminton. It’s a cool game. I think it’d really be your kind of thing. We should play.
Definitely. But I thought you were going there to do swimming.
Well, I wanted to try a swimming class like you did, but there weren’t any places left – you have to book in advance if it’s busy!
Oh, I didn’t realise that. Anyway, I like the sound of badminton.
We can go on Monday after school.
That sounds good.
Twelve. You will hear two friends talking about a party.
Mum says we can have the end-of-term class party at my house! She’s offered to do the food, too.
Remember, though, we’ve asked everyone to bring a dish. So it’s less work.
You’re right, I’d forgotten.
What about putting up balloons and coloured lights?
I’d prefer it if we talk to my parents about that – in case we damage something.
Like the walls, you mean? Probably best to ask, yeah. Anyway, I was thinking about the music. My brother’s got some awesome speakers. He’s going to show me how to connect a phone to them.
That sounds great. I can’t wait!
Thirteen. You will hear two friends talking about a football match.
Is it true that the coach didn’t choose you to play in the football match tomorrow?

Well, I had a long talk about it with her yesterday. The thing is, I haven’t been able to train as much as the other girls recently cos I hurt my leg in a match a few weeks ago. It’s OK, though. The coach knows I’ve nearly recovered, and it won’t be long before I’m back playing with the team again. I’m going to watch the others play tomorrow anyway to support them. I’d hate to miss seeing such a big match!
I’ll come, too.
That is the end of Part Two.
Now look at Part Three.
For each question, write the correct answer in the gap. Write one or two words or a number or a date or a time. Look at questions 14 to 19 now. You have 20 seconds.
You will hear a woman called Mona Dawson talking to a group of students about her work as a news reporter.

Hello, everybody. I’m here to tell you about my work as a news reporter. Some reporters study journalism at university, or subjects like politics and economics. I did history, and that’s really useful for understanding the world today.

After leaving university, I worked on a local newspaper, and got experience as a journalist. My first article actually went on the front page – but it was only about a new road. There weren’t many exciting events to write articles on, like, say, a bank robbery or celebrity wedding.

A news reporter must always be ready for a news story. Most reporters never go anywhere without a laptop, but I’m old-fashioned. I take a pen wherever I go, and I’ve lost my phone so many times! It’s useful to have some paper too, but I can always find something to write on.

Now I work on the news for a TV channel, and I sometimes interview famous people. The last one was a politician. I’ve just heard my next interview is with someone from a big transport company, but not the owner, or even a manager. Instead, it’s with a lorry driver. I’m sure it’ll be very interesting.

To be a TV reporter, lots of personal qualities are useful. Some people say a strong voice, others think it’s necessary to have a smart appearance. I’d say it’s my memory that really helps. It’s easy to forget things, so it’s essential to have a good one.

What about the future? I love writing and I’m planning a book. I’m interested in energy, and I believe we need to stop using oil so much. We know that the wind and the sea can produce energy, but the subject I’m going to explore is how we can use the sun to produce it for our needs.
Any questions … [fade]
That is the end of Part Three.
Now look at Part Four. For each question, choose the correct answer.
Look at questions 20 to 25 now. You have 45 seconds.
You will hear an interview with a young man called Matt Luxton, who worked as a volunteer at a rescue centre for sick elephants.
I’m talking to Matt Luxton who spent four weeks as a volunteer at a rescue centre for sick elephants. Matt, how did you learn about the rescue centre?

I’ve always loved elephants. My mum was worried about the idea of me going away when I told her about the organisation. It was one of my school teachers who’d shown me the advert for it. Luckily, my best friend supported me and helped me persuade Mum to let me go.
How did you pay for the trip?

Well, it wasn’t cheap. My uncle offered to lend me the money, but I wanted to pay for myself. A surfboard business had opened in town, and I got a job there. I thought about selling some of my things online, but I managed to save enough money without having to do that.
What was it like arriving at the elephant rescue centre?

It was evening when my plane landed and by the time I got to the rescue centre, all the elephants were asleep. The next day I was told there were over twenty of them! The welcome I got from the staff and the other volunteers was brilliant, I’ll never forget it. It was too dark to look around the gardens when I got there. I’ve got some great photos of the gorgeous trees and flowers that it’s known for.
What was your first job there?

It’s important to get used to the elephants slowly. So I could only watch when they were given a bath in the river – it looked such fun! Instead, I was asked to put all the stuff that the elephants were going to eat in buckets for them. I really wanted to work with the vets, who look after the elephants when they get sick, but you need qualifications for that.
What was difficult about the experience?

I thought the heat would be hard. It was OK, though. We woke up at sunrise ready to start work – it’s much cooler then. I met loads of people, but it wasn’t easy to understand what they were saying. Strange – I’m usually pretty good at languages. I wasn’t there long enough, I guess.
And what did you learn about elephants?

They’re wonderful creatures. I’d read so much about how clever they are, and what good memories they’ve got. But I just hadn’t realised that no two elephants are the same, until I’d spent time with them. One elephant might be brave, another quite shy, and another good at looking after the young. That’s what really impressed me.
Thanks, Matt … [fade]
That is the end of Part Four.
You now have six minutes to write your answers on the answer sheet.
You have one more minute.
That is the end of the test.
